full_judgment: 5. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and perused the revisional application, supplementary affidavit and counter-affidavits and other materials on record. It appears that the present petitioners as President, Secretary and other members of the Mutwalli Committee filed the instant application for addition of parties in the Miscellaneous Appeal stating that there was total mismanagement of the estate and the Mutwalli was incapable of running the estate properly. Accordingly, the petitioners, forming a committee for smooth running of the Waqf estate, sought for approval of the same to the Administrator of Waqfs who approved the said committee. It further appears that one Abdul Malek, the predecessor in-interest of the opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 as plaintiff claiming title in the land under dispute, brought the instant suit. Thereafter, one Moklesur Rahman was appointed as Receiver of the said property. Against which Hajera Bibi preferred appeal. At first petitioner No. 1 filed an application for addition of party which was rejected. The appellant Hajera Bibi by filing an application dated 7-10-1996 prayed for addition of the petitioners as parties in the instant appeal but the said application was rejected. Thereafter, the petitioners after getting appointment as office-bearers of Mutawalli committee from the Waqf Administrator filed application for addition of party in the instant proceeding. That is, they have brought this application in different capacity. The provision of Order I rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, empowers the court to implead any person as a party suo motu since if the plaintiff is permitted as a rule to choose his opponent, he may leave out the real owner and interested person and implead a person of his own choice and get a collusive decree which would have become final when real owner comes to know about it which will create an ugly situation. The parties having interest in the property are necessary parties in a proceeding. In this case it appears that the present petitioners have been appointed as office-bearers of the Mutwalli Committee by the Waqf Administrator in respect of the Waqf Estate so they have interest in the Waqf Estate. The High Court Division held the Mutwalli Committee appointed by the Waqf Administrator is a valid committee in Writ Petition No. 3903 or 1998. The appellant herself has no objection if the petitioners are impleaded as party in the instant proceeding. From the facts and circumstance of the case I am of the opinion that presence of the petitioners are necessary for effective and complete adjudication of the matter and to settle the controversy between the parties. So, I find substance in the submission made by Mr Khandaker Mahbubuddin. As it appears that the present petitioners have some interest in the instant property so I am of the view that they may be impleaded as respondents in the Miscellaneous Appeal pending before the Third Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka has failed to exercise his discretion properly as the petitioners have filed the application in different capacity.
